lumbar_numbering.hra: The library names six lumbar vertebrae L1-L6 counted from the rib-bearing T12 (spinal-cord-female v1.1: 'The Visible Human Female has 6 lumbar vertebrae'; united-female nodes VH_F_lumbar_vertebra_1..6, nucleus pulposus / disk 'of the first .. sixth lumbar vertebra' = the disk BELOW that vertebra).
lumbar_numbering.page: This page has six lumbar bodies (Q185k) and names them L1, L1B, L2, L3, L4, L5; the disc between L1 and L1B is not an atlas entity (Q185k2), so the page has 23 discs (C2-C3 .. L5-S1) where the HRA has 24.
lumbar_numbering.match: Rank-matched fits (7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 6 lumbar counted from the top, then refined by ICP) give a surface residual median 0.4-0.6 mm for every level incl. all six lumbar bodies: the page's six lumbar bodies ARE the HRA's L1-L6, one to one.
lumbar_numbering.consequence: HRA numbering is RIB-ANCHORED throughout and puts the extra vertebra at the bottom: HRA L2 = the page's L1B, HRA L3 = page L2, L4 = L3, L5 = L4, L6 = L5 (page L5-S1 disc = HRA L6-S1). The page's L2..L5 are off by one against the HRA (and against the usual convention) exactly as Q185k2 says; the page's L1 and the thoracic and cervical numbering agree.
lumbar_numbering.decision: No structure of the page is renamed (Q185k2 is an owner decision). The new nuclei carry the PAGE's disc names in their id and name (nucleus_pulposus_l2_l3 sits in intervertebral_disc_l2_l3) and say on the card which HRA disk it is; the HRA L1-L2 nucleus (page L1/L1B) is not shipped because the page has no disc there.
